answer: Each epoch, every identity must solve a copper-grade hashing puzzle whose difficulty scales with the number of identities sharing a funding source: 1 unit for a single account, plus 1 unit for each extra one. An operator running n accounts pays n(n+1)/2 units of compute, so the bridge from ten fakes to a hundred costs about 90 times more, not 10. Validators reach the summit of the check by recomputing 5 random solutions per epoch and zeroing rewards on any mismatch.
